gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro (4.13 lb, Macworld) weighs more than the 3.4 lb 14-inch MacBook Pro whose lid it hangs on: 4.13 ÷ 3.4 = 121% of the laptop's weight.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages, itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' and theofficejournal.com 'Best USB-C Laptop Screen Extenders', plus the top result, theofficejournal.com 'Best 14-Inch Laptop Screen Extenders'. None of them compares any extender's weight with a 14-inch laptop's weight. None gives a power draw in watts for the Trio 3 Pro or the Duex Max DS, a laptop-battery figure, or a screen area per pound. itechguides gives no weight for the Trio 3 Pro or the Duex Max DS. theofficejournal's 14-inch page gives no weights at all. Our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender is also in ChatGPT's results. It already gives the Duex Max DS 4.5 W and runtime hours against a 13-inch MacBook Air's 53.8 Wh battery, so the battery figure is only partly new. The weight-versus-14-inch-laptop figure is on none of the pages.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's single-screen pick for a 14-inch laptop. The Duex Max DS is rated at 4.5 W by Mobile Pixels, while the two-screen Trio 3 Pro weighs more than a 14-inch MacBook Pro (121%). That supports the page's 'less stress on the hinge' line: on a 14-inch laptop, put a lid-hung two-screen unit behind a freestanding one or the single Duex Max DS. Taken alone it does not pick a winner among the two-screen options, because I could not source weights for the FOPO S1 and S7 or the Aura Dual Boost 14 today. Fit note: our records give Mobile Pixels' own fit range for the Trio 3 Pro as 15–16 inches. Macworld tested it on a 14-inch MacBook Pro and lists 13–16-inch MacBooks.

findings.label: 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) weight
findings.note: Apple's figure for the base M6 14-inch model. The M5 Pro is 3.5 lb and the M5 Max is 3.6 lb. This is the reference 14-inch laptop for the ratios below.

findings.label: 14-inch MacBook Pro battery
findings.note: Apple lists the same 72.4 Wh lithium-polymer battery for the M6, M5 Pro and M5 Max 14-inch models.

findings.label: External displays, base 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Supports up to two external displays over any combination of Thunderbolt and HDMI ports.' So the base 14-inch Pro can drive two added screens natively, unlike base M1/M2/M3 MacBooks.

findings.label: Weight
findings.note: Macworld's figure. Macworld tested it on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, with two USB-C cables (one per screen), and needed no driver because the laptop has two DP-capable USB-C ports.

findings.label: Weight as a share of a 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld) + Apple MacBook Pro tech specs
findings.note: 4.13 lb (Macworld) ÷ 3.4 lb (Apple, https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/) = 1.21. The extender weighs about 0.7 lb more than the laptop it attaches to.

findings.label: Added screen area per pound
findings.note: Two 14.1-inch 16:10 panels: 14.1² × 160/356 = 89.3 sq in each, 178.7 sq in total. 178.7 ÷ 4.13 lb = 43.3 sq in/lb. Panel size and aspect ratio come from Mobile Pixels per our product record; the weight is Macworld's.

findings.label: Power on laptop power alone
findings.value: No external supply needed; brightness capped below maximum
findings.note: Macworld: the screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness.' Plugging an adapter into a Trio USB-C port raises brightness and passes up to 65 W to the laptop, which needs the driver. Macworld gives no wattage for the draw.

findings.label: Energy consumption (maker rating)
findings.note: Mobile Pixels' spec page: 14.1-inch, 1920×1080, 300 nit, 12.6 × 8.9 × 0.25 in at the thinnest point. The page gives no weight.

findings.label: Share of a 14-inch MacBook Pro's battery used over an 8-hour day
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Max specs + Apple MacBook Pro tech specs
findings.note: 4.5 W × 8 h = 36 Wh. 36 ÷ 72.4 Wh (Apple) = 0.497. This counts the screen's rated draw only, so it excludes the laptop's own use and conversion loss. Equivalent: 72.4 ÷ 4.5 = 16.1 h of screen-only draw from a full battery.

findings.label: Added screen area
findings.note: 14.1-inch 16:9 panel: 14.1² × 144/337 = 84.9 sq in. For comparison, the Trio 3 Pro's two panels add 178.7 sq in.
